items.subsection: Decision Models, Routing, and the “Jev” Wave
items.title: Discriminative models broke out as a new systems primitive
items.summary: The biggest technical conversation was around Jev , a non-generative decision model being positioned as a fast “ System 1 ” complement to LLMs.

items.subsection: Decision Models, Routing, and the “Jev” Wave
items.title: Open reproductions and ecosystem clones appeared immediately
items.summary: @madiator released Bespoke Nimble , an “open Jev” recipe built from a LoRA fine-tune of Qwen3.5-9B using synthetic contrastive data curation and constrained decoding.

items.subsection: Decision Models, Routing, and the “Jev” Wave
items.title: The first compelling integrations were in browser/computer-use workflows
items.summary: @levie demoed Jev classifying Box incident reports into escalation paths; @ndrezn showed browser use with LangChain + Jev and found it strong on tasks like the Wikipedia game and structured “folding laundry” workflows; @cline shipped a plugin giving Jev a brow…

items.subsection: Agent Tooling, Coding Harnesses, and Claude Code Standards
items.title: AGENTS.md gained real momentum as a cross-tool convention
items.summary: The highest-signal product update here was @trq212 announcing that Claude Code v2.1.277 now checks for AGENTS.md when no CLAUDE.md is present, with config-level toggle support.

items.subsection: Agent Tooling, Coding Harnesses, and Claude Code Standards
items.title: Harness design is becoming a first-class variable in coding-agent performance and cost
items.summary: @pidotdev highlighted the Harness Tax analysis showing that a simple tool set— read, write, edit, bash —can reach the Pareto frontier on benchmark performance while reducing unnecessary spending.

items.subsection: Agent Tooling, Coding Harnesses, and Claude Code Standards
items.title: Model choice in software systems is bifurcating
items.summary: Several practitioners described a split between “frontier for planning, cheap for execution.” @TheAhmadOsman summarized one stack as GPT 5.6 Sol XHigh for planning, GLM 5.3 Flash for implementation, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash for other tasks.

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Recursive Self-Improvement, and Math Capability
items.title: RSI discussion got more precise about what is actually “recursive”
items.summary: @TheTuringPost offered a useful taxonomy: AI improving code or training methods is not, by itself, fully recursive if the surrounding improvement loop remains fixed.

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Recursive Self-Improvement, and Math Capability
items.title: Math benchmarks continued to fall to frontier models, but interpretation remains nuanced
items.summary: @EpochAIResearch reported that another FrontierMath open problem was solved in an interactive session with GPT-6 Astra . Separately, @SAIRfoundation launched Open Math Model , pitching open models and tools for mathematics shaped by the research community.

items.subsection: Benchmarks, Recursive Self-Improvement, and Math Capability
items.title: Computer-use benchmarks are still far from saturation
items.summary: @ValsAI launched CUA-Bench , testing real-time keyboard/mouse use across 6 games (with 3 kept private ) as a proxy for difficult human-easy tasks. Follow-up numbers from @ValsAI suggest this remains genuinely hard: all frontier models score below 20% .

items.subsection: Infra, Training Systems, and Model Architecture
items.title: Long-context and large-scale training infrastructure remain active optimization fronts
items.summary: @Azaliamirh released Turbo-dLLM , an open-source library for training diffusion LLMs at scale, reporting 2.48x speedup at 512K context and 7.59x at 1M context on 8x H100s via Context-Sharded Block Parallelism .

items.subsection: Infra, Training Systems, and Model Architecture
items.title: Architecture taxonomy debates are still alive
items.summary: @ahatamiz1 argued that the field is overusing SSM as a label for any linear model. His proposal is to use linear RNNs as the umbrella term, with SSMs as one sub-family, distinguishing systems like Mamba2 from the GDN family on the basis that GDN behaves more l…

items.subsection: Infra, Training Systems, and Model Architecture
items.title: Edge/local neural program execution also got a notable update
items.summary: @yuntiandeng described ProgramAsWeights , where developers specify an AI function in English, compile it once, and then run a small neural program locally on CPU with Wi‑Fi off . The code and models are public.

items.subsection: Robotics, Vision, Audio, and Generative Media
items.title: Open robotics data releases were unusually substantive
items.summary: @adamrasb announced the full ABC release, including code, 400+ hours of sim data on 24 tasks , and 5,850 labeled policy-evaluation episodes .

items.subsection: Robotics, Vision, Audio, and Generative Media
items.title: Astra is showing up across evals and products, especially for vision
items.summary: @skalskip92 reported GPT-6 Astra as the strongest vision model Roboflow has tested across detection, segmentation, box prompting, counting, reasoning, and video.

items.subsection: Robotics, Vision, Audio, and Generative Media
items.title: Speech and lip-sync saw strong benchmarked releases
items.summary: @ArtificialAnlys reported Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0 reaching 2.7% WER on streaming final transcripts at 0.49s after end-of-speech, improving from 3.9% on its predecessor while keeping pricing at $0.20/hour streaming and $0.10/hour non-streaming .

items.subsection: AI Safety, Evaluation Governance, and Security
items.title: Anthropic’s evaluator-embedding strategy became more concrete—and more controversial
items.summary: @AnthropicAI announced a partnership with Accenture on independent evaluation of frontier AI , saying the two organizations expect to invest at least $1B over five years to build capacity.

items.subsection: AI Safety, Evaluation Governance, and Security
items.title: The “rogue agents” / Hugging Face incident continued to drive debate about containment
items.summary: @polynoamial clarified that his much-mocked thought experiment was about coordination between supposedly isolated agents , not weight exfiltration via thermal sensors, and argued the lesson from the HF incident is to avoid trusting sandbox isolation as a sole…

items.subsection: AI Safety, Evaluation Governance, and Security
items.title: Policy pressure is building around safety laws and operational accountability
items.summary: @TheRundownAI reported that California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed an executive order convening an expert panel to recommend stronger AI safety laws, including possible kill switches , embedded outside monitors, and required safety plans.

items.title: Introducing the Australian Youth Safety Blueprint
items.summary: OpenAI introduces the Australian Youth Safety Blueprint, a six-pillar roadmap for safer AI experiences that protect and empower young people.
